package_info.package_versions: All UI builds deployed to IPFS since January 1, 2024
package_info.why_malicious: A developer inserted malicious JavaScript into the Tornado Cash user interface, which covertly exfiltrated users’ private deposit notes to an external server, enabling theft of funds. This was a supply chain attack targeting users accessing the service via IPFS gateways.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (user interaction with Tornado Cash UI)
execution_context.file_location: JavaScript code in the Tornado Cash web UI (deployed via IPFS gateways)
required_permissions: access to in-browser cryptographic secrets (deposit notes)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code intercepts the user's private deposit note during normal UI operations, encodes it, and sends it via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled server, enabling secret exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exfiltrates sensitive cryptographic secrets (deposit notes) to an external server, which is not required for legitimate mixer operation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Tornado Cash UI code should never transmit private deposit notes or cryptographic secrets off-device; all cryptographic operations should remain local to the user's browser.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate telemetry or analytics might send non-sensitive usage data, but never private keys or deposit notes.
key_indicators: Access to cryptographic secrets (deposit notes) in client-side code
Network request to external, non-Tornado Cash server
Encoding and transmission of sensitive data during normal UI operations

attack_chain.action: Malicious developer submits a governance proposal containing backdoored JavaScript code to the Tornado Cash open-source repository.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is merged and deployed to IPFS gateways.

attack_chain.action: Compromised UI is served to users via IPFS gateways (e.g., ipfs.io, cf-ipfs.com).
attack_chain.leads_to: Users interact with the malicious UI.

attack_chain.action: When users perform deposit or withdrawal actions, the malicious code captures their private deposit notes.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive deposit notes are exfiltrated to the attacker's server.

attack_chain.action: Attacker collects exfiltrated deposit notes and uses them to withdraw or steal funds from Tornado Cash contracts.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: theft of user funds and compromise of privacy.

behavioral_signatures: Client-side JavaScript accessing cryptographic secrets (deposit notes/private keys)
Outbound network requests from the UI to non-official, external domains during normal user operations
Encoding and transmission of sensitive data (e.g., via encodeURIComponent or base64) in network payloads
file_indicators: Unexpected or obfuscated JavaScript code in Tornado Cash UI builds
References to external domains not associated with Tornado Cash in UI source code
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests from user browsers to attacker-controlled domains (not tornado.cash or official infrastructure)
Unusual traffic patterns from IPFS-hosted Tornado Cash UIs to unknown endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Tornado Cash UI builds for unauthorized JavaScript code that accesses deposit notes or cryptographic secrets and sends them to external servers. Use static and dynamic analysis to flag any code that transmits sensitive data off-device. Network monitoring should alert on POST requests from Tornado Cash UIs to non-official domains. Regularly audit governance proposals and code contributions for hidden or obfuscated data exfiltration logic.
